title: Underwater
description: Underwater cinematography leaves air: the camera is in water, so caustics, buoyancy, and a missing horizon rewrite every edge. The medium is the matter; particles are silt and bubbles, and bodies move as if the world had gone slow without a slow-motion shutter.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Hair and cloth delay. Light arrives as moving lattice from a surface that is now a ceiling.
There is no standing horizon, only up toward silver and down toward dark. Leave air.

Use it when the scene is actually submerged: a pool, a sea, a tank, a flood. It is the wrong tool when you only want grace: dry Slow Motion with a blue grade is a lie, and it shows in hair that still falls at air speed.
It is the wrong tool when the story is on the swell with a sky: that is Ocean. Color dies with depth (reds first).
If the red dress is still loud at ten meters, you stayed in air.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Put the lens in a housing in water (or a convincing tank). Expose for caustics from the real sun or a hard source through the surface.
Let bubbles and silt backlight. Wardrobe and hair must float.
Camera moves fight drag; they read slower. Prompt: underwater of [Subject], caustics, muffled space, hair and cloth in slow water, a world without horizon.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for a dive, a drowning, a creature, a flooded corridor. Do not use it as a look for a dry bedroom.
If you need the surface and the sky, shoot ocean, then go under for a beat if the story dives.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Ocean is the surface world: swell, horizon, salt light. Atmospheric Haze is air scatter.
Slow Motion is a frame-rate choice that often accompanies underwater but is not the medium. Underwater is a different optical path: refraction, caustics, buoyancy, no air horizon.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The Big Blue lives in the medium, not in a tint. The Shape of Water makes tanks and canals a second gravity.
Thunderball proved action can be staged as true submerged geography. Use caustics and float, not a teal LUT on a dry actor.

sections.title: Prompt it

blocks.text: Underwater of [Subject], caustics, muffled space, hair and cloth in slow water, a world without horizon. Name depth, the surface as ceiling or absence, floating wardrobe, silt or bubbles in backlight.
For video, buoyancy and drag; no air-speed hair, no standing horizon unless looking up at the underside of the surface.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a blue grade in air, or Ocean from a boat. The tell: cloth hangs, hair falls, a skyline, no caustics.
The fix: submerge the camera, float the fabrics, add caustics and backlit silt, kill the air horizon.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Underwater in film?
Underwater work puts camera and subject in water, so caustics, buoyancy, particles, and a missing air horizon rewrite the frame. The medium is the atmosphere.
Underwater vs Ocean
Ocean is the surface: swell, sky, a horizon that can kill you. Underwater leaves that sky and treats the surface as a ceiling. One is a seascape; the other is a different world.
When should I use Underwater?
Use it when the scene is submerged. Do not use a blue grade or slow motion in air as a substitute, and do not call a boat horizon underwater.
How do I prompt Underwater for AI image or video?
Demand caustics, floating cloth, and no air horizon. Example: underwater of [Subject], caustics, muffled space, hair and cloth in slow water. Specify silt or bubbles in backlight.
